q: How are precursor emissions added for Ha Tinh blast furnace steel under CBAM?
title: Ha Tinh BF-BOF steel: adding precursors
short: Embedded emissions of the steel are the direct emissions of the steelmaking step plus the embedded emissions of each relevant precursor used, such as pig iron and sintered ore, per tonne of product. Electricity is not added for iron and steel, because only direct emissions are charged for these goods.
audience: Integrated blast furnace and converter steel producers in the Ha Tinh and Nghi Son corridor of Vietnam and their EU importers

p: Find the direct emissions of the converter and downstream steps in the period.
For each precursor used, multiply the tonnes consumed by its embedded emissions per tonne.
Add the two and divide by the tonnes of the CBAM good produced.
For crude steel the relevant precursors include pig iron, DRI, ferroalloys and, where made on site, sintered ore. Each carries its own embedded emissions, worked out the same way one step earlier.
Indirect emissions from electricity are not charged for iron and steel in the definitive period, though they are still reported for information where the rules ask for it.

example.title: Worked example: one tonne of steel (illustrative inputs)
lines: Pig iron used: 0.95 t x 1.90 t CO2 per t = 1.805 t CO2
Direct emissions of the converter step: 0.10 t CO2
Embedded emissions: 1.805 + 0.10 = 1.905 t CO2 per t of steel
example.note: The pig iron figure and the converter figure are illustrative; use your installation's monitored values.
